periods.analysis: Behavioral health screening began at the Community Health Center and Public Health clinics, with 238 residents referred. The first 41 staff finished mental health literacy training and nine organizations signed the coordination agreement. Knowledge gains of 17 points were lower than we wanted, so the course is being revised.
periods.recommendations: Shorten the literacy course, extend screening to hospital discharge planning, and begin drafting shared intake forms.

periods.analysis: Referrals rose to 341 after Bayview Medical Center discharge planners began screening, and 77 staff have now completed literacy training with gains improving to 21 points. The agreement has 12 signers, but only four serve higher-risk groups, which we are watching closely.
periods.recommendations: Open the warm-handoff line, train dispatch and Parks cohorts, and move the shared intake form into legal review.

periods.analysis: Screening-and-referral volume rose from 238 in Q1 to 462 in Q3, and 118 City and partner staff have completed mental health literacy training. The coordination agreement now has 15 signers. The agreement still needs more signatories who work directly with higher-risk groups, which is the main item for Q4.
periods.recommendations: Finish legal review of the shared intake forms and add signers who serve higher-risk groups.
